title.narrative: Reducing the Health Impacts of E-Waste Recycling in Accra, Ghana

description.narrative: This project will conduct research to protect the health of residents of Accra, Ghana, by reducing their exposure to environmental toxins released by the improper burning and recycling of electric and electronic waste products. The burning and breaking of e-wastes (in order to salvage cooper and other valuable metals) exposes both workers and their communities to hazardous levels of lead, dioxins, and other poisons. Additionally, this project will research ways to protect livelihoods of those engaged in e-waste recycling. This project will contribute to poverty reduction, social inclusion, and social protection of informal e-waste workers by investigating initiatives that will reduce occupational exposures to toxins. Through research, this project seeks to develop and promote the adoption of best practices to increase the economic viability of e-waste recycling. Specific results will include: 1. An active stakeholder group that advocates for the interests of the community, with government health agencies and environmental regulators 2. A baseline assessment of toxic exposures amongst workers and their families 3. Raised awareness of the risks of improper techniques amongst workers 4. The research of best management practices to equip e-waste workers to safely handle and recycle e-waste
